Mr. Neeraj Srivastava, Advocate has put in appearance on behalf of first informant/opposite party-2.

However, neither any counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of first informant/opposite party-2 nor the learned counsel representing opposite party-2 or anyone on his behalf is present to oppose this repeat application for bail.

6. The first bail application of applicant was rejected by this Court by a detailed order dated 21.08.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 34105 of 2023 (Bantu Vs. State of U.P.

sentences.text:
For ready reference, the said order is reproduced herein under:
"Heard Mr. Kamalendra Kumar Maurya, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr. Neeraj Srivastava, the learned counsel for first informant opposite party 2.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant Bantu seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 295 of 2022, under Sections 363, 376, 120B IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S. Fatehabad, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.

Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 17.12.2022, a delayed F.I.R. dated 19.12.2022 was lodged by first informant Smt.
Balkumari (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No. 295 of 2022, under Sections 363, 376, 120B IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S.
Fatehabad, District Agra.
In the aforesaid F.I.R., applicant Bantu has been nominated as solitary named accused.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated in above mentioned case crime number.
Referring to the statements of the prosecutrix as recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr. P. C.
It is urged that prima facie prosecutrix is a consenting party.
As such, no offence as alleged can be said to have been committed by the applicant.
Medical evidence does not support the ocular version of the occurrence.
Applicant is in jail since 04.01.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than 7 months of incarceration.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents, inasmuch he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
On the basis of above, it is urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.

sentences.text: 2 Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel for first informant have opposed the present application for bail.

They submit that on the date of occurrence,
the prosecutrix was a young girl below the age of 16 years as per her date of birth recorded in the High School Certificate.

Placing reliance upon the judgement of the Supreme Court in X (Minor) Vs. State of Jharkhand, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 194, the learned A.G.A. contends that since the prosecutrix was below 16 years on the date of occurrence, therefore, the consent, if any of the prosecutrix is wholly immaterial.

entities.text: X (Minor) Vs. State of Jharkhand, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 194
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is urged by the learned A.G.A. that in the light of law laid down by the Apex Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74, it is by now well settled that the prosecution of an accused for an offence of sexual assault can be maintained even on the statement of the solitary evidence of prosecutrix.

entities.text: Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in such a circumstance, the statement of the prosecutrix must be clear, categorical and consistent.
When the aforesaid test is applied to the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr. P. C., it cannot be said that her statements are inconsistent or contradictory.
It is thus urged that when the statement of the prosecutrix are taken as a whole, they fall in the category of impeccable evidence.
On the above premise, it is thus urged that irrespective of the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant, no sympathy be shown by this Court.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial in favour of applicant.

When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.
Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for state, learned counsel for first informant, upon perusal of material brought on record, nature and gravity of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, accusation made and coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix is a young girl aged about 15 years 11months and 10 days on the date of occurrence, therefore, consent, if any, of the prosecutrix is immaterial, the judgement of Supreme Court in X (Minor) Vs. State of Jharkhand (supra), therefore, irrespective of the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail,
As a result the bail application fails and is liable to be rejected.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that subsequent to above order dated 21.08.2023, the trial of applicant commenced before court below by means of aforementioned sessions trial.
The first informant has deposed before court below as P.W.-1 whereas the prosecutrix has deposed before court below as P.W.-2.
However, the prosecutrix in her deposition before court below has not supported the F.I.R.
Accordingly, the prosecutrix has been declared hostile.

On the above premise,
the learned counsel for applicant submits that since the statements of first informant and that of the Bantu vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76182803/
3 prosecutrix have been recorded before court below, who have not supported the F.IR., therefore in case the applicant is enlarged on bail then in that eventuality it cannot be said that if the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall either terrorize the witnesses or shall hamper the course of trial.

entities.text: Bantu vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore, once the prosecutrix has not supported the F.I.R. in her deposition before court below, no justifiable ground now exists to prolong the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
8. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in custody since 04.01.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than one year and ten months of incarceration.

The police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallised.
However, upto this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the cumulative strength of above, he submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
9. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed this repeat application for bail.
Learned A.G.A. submits that since the applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, no indulgence be granted by this Court in favour of applicant.

However, the learned A.G.A. could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this repeat application for bail with reference to the record at this stage.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and upon consideration of material on record, evidence, gravity and nature of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant, coupled with the fact that the statements of first informant and that of the prosecutrix have already been recorded before court below, the prosecutrix in her deposition before court below has not supported the F.I.R., accordingly the prosecutrix has been declared hostile, in view of above, if the applicant is enlarged on bail then in that eventuality it cannot be said that if the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall either terrorize the witnesses or shall hamper the course of trial, once the prosecutrix has herself not supported the F.I.R., no good ground now exists to prolong the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the police report (charge sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C has already been submitted against applicant therefore the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized, yet in spite of above, no such incriminating circumstance could be pointed out by learned the A.G.A.
from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the judgement of Apex Court in Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (Paragraph 6), the clean antecedents of applicant, the period of incarceration undergone, therefore irrespective of the objections raised by learned A.G.A. in opposition to this repeat application for bail but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (Paragraph 6)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. Accordingly, present repeat application for bail is allowed.

sentences.text:
12. Let the applicant-Bantu involved in aforesaid case crime number be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) Applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence.
(ii) Applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) Applicant will not indulge in any unlawful activities.
(iv) Applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

13. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant and send him to prison.
Order Date :- 11.11.2024 YK  Bantu vs State Of U.P.And 3 Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76182803/
